questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Working the problem, reducing a nitrile, R-CN, to a primary amine, R-CH2NH2, adds how many hydrogen atoms in total?

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Explain the following: why does aqueous amine basicity not simply follow alkyl substitution?

answer.exemplar: Alkyl groups donate electron density and raise intrinsic basicity, but aqueous basicity also depends on how well the resulting ammonium ion is solvated by water; increasing substitution improves donation but worsens solvation, so the balance often makes secondary amines the most basic in water while tertiary amines can be less basic than expected.

questions.explanation: Solvation offsets inductive donation. Alkyl groups donate electron density and raise intrinsic basicity, but aqueous basicity also depends on how well the resulting ammonium ion is solvated by water; increasing substitution improves donation but worsens solvation, so the balance often makes secondary amines the most basic in water while tertiary amines can be less basic than expected.
questions.hint: Gas phase follows donation more closely.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Explain the following: why is the lone pair of aniline less available for protonation?

answer.exemplar: The nitrogen lone pair overlaps with the pi system of the benzene ring and is delocalized into the ring in resonance contributors that place negative charge at ortho and para positions; because the lone pair is spread out and partly used in bonding to the ring, it is less available to accept a proton than a localized alkylamine lone pair.

questions.explanation: Delocalization stabilizes the free base. The nitrogen lone pair overlaps with the pi system of the benzene ring and is delocalized into the ring in resonance contributors that place negative charge at ortho and para positions; because the lone pair is spread out and partly used in bonding to the ring, it is less available to accept a proton than a localized alkylamine lone pair.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Explain the following: why is reductive amination preferred over direct alkylation of ammonia?

answer.exemplar: Reductive amination forms the carbon-nitrogen bond by condensation of a carbonyl with an amine followed by selective reduction, and because the amine component can be used in controlled stoichiometry and the imine is reduced as it forms, overalkylation is minimized compared with repeated SN2 alkylation of ammonia.

questions.explanation: Imine reduction gives controlled monoalkylation. Reductive amination forms the carbon-nitrogen bond by condensation of a carbonyl with an amine followed by selective reduction, and because the amine component can be used in controlled stoichiometry and the imine is reduced as it forms, overalkylation is minimized compared with repeated SN2 alkylation of ammonia.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Explain the following: why does the Gabriel synthesis give a clean primary amine?

answer.exemplar: Phthalimide anion is alkylated once because the nitrogen in the product imide is no longer strongly nucleophilic, so a second alkylation cannot occur; subsequent hydrolysis or hydrazinolysis then frees the primary amine while leaving the alkyl group intact.

answer.exemplar: Reductive amination forms the carbon-nitrogen bond by condensation of a carbonyl with an amine followed by selective reduction, and because the amine component can be used in controlled stoichiometry and the imine is reduced as it forms, overalkylation is minimized compared with repeated SN2 alkylation of ammonia.

questions.stem: Explain the chemistry: why does the Gabriel synthesis give a clean primary amine?

answer.exemplar: Phthalimide anion is alkylated once because the nitrogen in the product imide is no longer strongly nucleophilic, so a second alkylation cannot occur; subsequent hydrolysis or hydrazinolysis then frees the primary amine while leaving the alkyl group intact.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Discuss the reasoning: why does aqueous amine basicity not simply follow alkyl substitution?

answer.exemplar: Alkyl groups donate electron density and raise intrinsic basicity, but aqueous basicity also depends on how well the resulting ammonium ion is solvated by water; increasing substitution improves donation but worsens solvation, so the balance often makes secondary amines the most basic in water while tertiary amines can be less basic than expected.

questions.explanation: Solvation offsets inductive donation. questions.hint: Gas phase follows donation more closely.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Discuss the reasoning: why is the lone pair of aniline less available for protonation?

answer.exemplar: The nitrogen lone pair overlaps with the pi system of the benzene ring and is delocalized into the ring in resonance contributors that place negative charge at ortho and para positions; because the lone pair is spread out and partly used in bonding to the ring, it is less available to accept a proton than a localized alkylamine lone pair.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Analyzing the data, which substituent makes phenol more acidic?

options.text: A methyl group para to the hydroxyl
options.misconception: methyl donates and weakens the acid

options.text: A methoxy group para to the hydroxyl
options.misconception: methoxy donates by resonance and weakens the acid

options.text: A tert-butyl group para to the hydroxyl
A nitro group para to the hydroxyl

questions.explanation: Electron-withdrawing groups such as nitro stabilize the phenoxide conjugate base by resonance and induction when ortho or para, lowering the pKa; electron-donating groups destabilize phenoxide and raise it.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Analyzing the data, which structural feature is required for an aryl halide to undergo SNAr addition-elimination?

options.text: Strong electron-withdrawing groups ortho or para to the halide
An electron-donating group para to the halide

options.misconception: meta cannot stabilize the Meisenheimer complex

questions.explanation: The addition-elimination SNAr mechanism requires electron-withdrawing groups ortho or para to the leaving group to stabilize the anionic Meisenheimer intermediate by resonance; meta groups cannot provide that stabilization.
questions.hint: Ortho or para electron withdrawal stabilizes the intermediate.

questions.stem: Analyzing the data, what unusual product distribution indicates a benzyne mechanism?

options.misconception: benzyne gives substitution at either benzyne carbon

options.text: Substitution at the carbon adjacent to the original halogen

questions.explanation: Under very strong base an aryl halide eliminates to a benzyne intermediate, and nucleophile addition to either carbon of the strained triple bond gives a mixture that can include substitution at the carbon neighboring the original halogen, called cine substitution.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Analyzing the data, why is phenol highly activated toward electrophilic aromatic substitution?

options.text: The hydroxyl withdraws electrons inductively only
The hydroxyl donates a lone pair by resonance into the ring
The hydroxyl is a strong leaving group
options.misconception: that is not relevant to EAS

questions.explanation: The oxygen lone pair donates into the aromatic pi system, increasing electron density especially at ortho and para positions and stabilizing the sigma complex, which strongly activates the ring toward electrophilic attack.
questions.hint: Resonance donation activates ortho and para.

questions.stem: Based on the evidence, why is phenol highly activated toward electrophilic aromatic substitution?

options.text: The hydroxyl donates a lone pair by resonance into the ring
The hydroxyl withdraws electrons inductively only
The hydroxyl is a strong leaving group
options.misconception: that is not relevant to EAS

questions.explanation: The oxygen lone pair donates into the aromatic pi system, increasing electron density especially at ortho and para positions and stabilizing the sigma complex, which strongly activates the ring toward electrophilic attack.
questions.hint: Resonance donation activates ortho and para.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Based on the evidence, which two partners are coupled in a Suzuki reaction?

options.text: An aryl boronic acid and an aryl halide
An aryl Grignard and an aryl halide
An aryl hydrazine and an aldehyde

questions.explanation: The Suzuki reaction couples an organoboron compound such as an aryl boronic acid with an aryl halide or triflate under palladium catalysis and base, forming a new carbon-carbon bond between the two aryl groups.
questions.hint: Boronic acid plus aryl halide under palladium.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Based on the evidence, heating an aqueous acidic aryl diazonium salt gives which product?
questions.explanation: Warming an aqueous acidic diazonium salt replaces the diazonium group with hydroxyl, releasing nitrogen gas and giving a phenol through a carbocation-like intermediate captured by water.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Based on the evidence, which reagent cleaves an aryl methyl ether to give a phenol?

options.misconception: base does not cleave aryl methyl ethers
that does not cleave the ether

options.text: Concentrated hydrobromic acid or boron tribromide

questions.explanation: Aryl methyl ethers are cleaved by strong acids such as concentrated HBr or by boron tribromide; cleavage occurs at the alkyl oxygen bond because aryl-oxygen bonds are too strong for SN2 attack.
questions.hint: Boron tribromide or strong acid removes methyl ethers.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Based on the evidence, what is the structure of benzyne?

options.text: A benzene ring with an additional triple bond between adjacent carbons
A benzene ring with a radical
options.misconception: benzyne has a strained triple bond

options.text: A benzene ring bearing a carbocation

questions.explanation: Benzyne is benzene with an extra pi bond between two adjacent carbons, forming a very strained alkyne within the ring that is highly reactive toward nucleophilic addition.
questions.hint: Benzyne has a strained ring triple bond.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Based on the evidence, in SNAr on an activated aryl halide, which halogen is generally the best leaving group?

options.misconception: unlike SN1, fluorine is best in SNAr

questions.explanation: In SNAr the rate-determining step is addition of the nucleophile, and the strongly electron-withdrawing fluorine atom stabilizes the Meisenheimer intermediate by induction, making aryl fluorides unexpectedly reactive despite the strong carbon-fluorine bond.
questions.hint: Fluorine is best in SNAr addition-elimination.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Based on the evidence, where is the negative charge of phenoxide delocalized?

options.misconception: phenoxide has resonance contributors into the ring
resonance places charge at ortho and para

options.text: Onto the ortho and para carbons of the ring

questions.explanation: The phenoxide anion delocalizes its negative charge from oxygen into the ring at the ortho and para positions through resonance contributors, which stabilizes the anion and accounts for the acidity of phenols.
questions.hint: Charge appears at ortho and para ring carbons.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In a practice exercise, which substituent makes phenol more acidic?

options.text: A methyl group para to the hydroxyl
options.misconception: methyl donates and weakens the acid

options.text: A methoxy group para to the hydroxyl
options.misconception: methoxy donates by resonance and weakens the acid

options.text: A tert-butyl group para to the hydroxyl
A nitro group para to the hydroxyl

questions.explanation: Electron-withdrawing groups such as nitro stabilize the phenoxide conjugate base by resonance and induction when ortho or para, lowering the pKa; electron-donating groups destabilize phenoxide and raise it.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In a practice exercise, which structural feature is required for an aryl halide to undergo SNAr addition-elimination?

options.text: Strong electron-withdrawing groups ortho or para to the halide
An electron-donating group para to the halide

options.misconception: meta cannot stabilize the Meisenheimer complex

questions.explanation: The addition-elimination SNAr mechanism requires electron-withdrawing groups ortho or para to the leaving group to stabilize the anionic Meisenheimer intermediate by resonance; meta groups cannot provide that stabilization.
questions.hint: Ortho or para electron withdrawal stabilizes the intermediate.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In a practice exercise, what unusual product distribution indicates a benzyne mechanism?

options.misconception: benzyne gives substitution at either benzyne carbon

options.text: Substitution at the carbon adjacent to the original halogen

questions.explanation: Under very strong base an aryl halide eliminates to a benzyne intermediate, and nucleophile addition to either carbon of the strained triple bond gives a mixture that can include substitution at the carbon neighboring the original halogen, called cine substitution.
